findings.title: Error from CDN read is discarded when falling back to file read
findings.body: In GetWebAssets, when `cdn != ""` the code calls `readWebAssetsFromCDN` and assigns the result to `err`, but then at line 59 the condition `if result == nil` unconditionally overwrites `err` by calling `readWebAssetsFromFile`. If the CDN read failed with a meaningful error (network failure, malformed manifest, etc.), that error is silently lost and replaced by the file-read error (or nil if the file read succeeds). This makes debugging CDN failures impossible and can mask the real cause when the file fallback also fails or when the CDN error would have been more informative. The original `err` from the CDN path should be preserved or combined (e.g., using errors.Join or returning the CDN error when the file fallback also fails).

findings.title: Cache is populated even when asset loading failed, poisoning subsequent calls
findings.body: At line 69, `entryPointAssetsCache = result` is executed unconditionally, even when `result` is nil due to an error from `readWebAssetsFromFile` (or the CDN path). On the next call in a non-dev environment, the fast path at lines 41-47 checks `ret != nil` — since the cache is nil, it will retry, which is acceptable. However, the more serious issue is that when `readWebAssetsFromFile` returns a non-nil result but also a non-nil error (which shouldn't happen per the function signature contract, but the code doesn't guard against it), or more importantly: if `result` is nil and `err` is non-nil, the cache remains nil and every subsequent request in production will re-attempt the expensive file read (or CDN fetch) on every call, causing repeated disk I/O or network requests under load. There is no negative caching or error short-circuiting. Additionally, if a transient error occurs (e.g., file temporarily unavailable), the system will hammer the filesystem on every request until success, with no backoff or caching of the failure state.

findings.title: TOCTOU race between cache check and lock acquisition allows duplicate work
findings.body: The double-checked locking pattern at lines 41-49 has a benign race: between the RUnlock at line 43 and the Lock at line 48, another goroutine may have already populated the cache. This goroutine will then acquire the write lock and redundantly re-read the assets from disk/CDN, even though the cache is now valid. This is not a correctness bug (the mutex ensures memory safety), but it means that under high concurrency during cold start, multiple goroutines can simultaneously perform expensive I/O operations (file reads, potential CDN fetches) instead of just one. A proper double-checked locking pattern would re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock: `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock(); if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock(); return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }; defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()`. This would prevent thundering-herd duplicate work.

findings.title: Return value reads cache variable instead of local result, which is equivalent but confusing
findings.body: Line 70 returns `entryPointAssetsCache` (the global) rather than the local `result` variable. While functionally equivalent since line 69 just assigned `result` to the global, this is fragile: if the assignment at line 69 were ever changed or reordered, the return value would diverge from what was just computed. More importantly, returning the global after releasing the lock (via defer) means the caller receives a pointer to shared mutable state without any guarantee that another goroutine won't mutate it (though dtos.EntryPointAssets appears to be treated as immutable after construction). Returning the local `result` would be clearer and safer: `return result, err`.
